question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 02 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The change in db.pool_size caused the connection pool to be exhausted, leading to increased latency.
why_chain: The db.pool_size was reduced from 50 to 5, causing the connection pool to be exhausted.
With fewer connections available, the checkout service experienced longer waits for connections.
This resulted in increased latency, as the service had to wait for connections to become available.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume did not explain the increase in latency.
why_chain: The request volume for service checkout did not change significantly.
The error rate increased, indicating issues within the service itself, not just increased load.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a sudden spike in traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume did not change significantly, and the error rate increased, not decreased.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence suggests the service was affected by an external service failure or slowdown.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for service checkout rose from 222 ms to 579 ms (+161%), with a change point at 2026-03-02T10:50:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service checkout: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for service checkout stayed about the same (817 per 5 min before, 1013 per 5 min after, +24%).
At the same time, error rate for service checkout rose (0.36% before, 0.53% after, +49%).
Changed checkout db.pool_size from 50 to 5 (all regions) (checkout; 1 min before the change; record R014)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, ap-south; 2 min after the change; record R015)
p95 latency above SLO on checkout (checkout; 15 min after the change; record R018)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, eu-west; 8 min after the change; record R016)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, us-east; 14 min after the change; record R017)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (1 min before the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Increase the db.pool_size back to 50 to ensure the connection pool is not exhausted.
Implement a mechanism to monitor and alert on connection pool exhaustion.
Review and optimize the checkout service's connection management to reduce the likelihood of connection pool exhaustion.
